hints.title: Use the axis of symmetry
hints.body: Complete the square with the leading coefficient left as a parameter, or use the vertex-input formula. Match the horizontal coordinate to the given axis.
hints.recap: The symmetry axis passes through the vertex of a quadratic.
hints.pitfall: Account for the coefficient of the squared term when finding the vertex.
hints.pause: Use the axis to form an equation for the leading coefficient.

recall.reminder: The symmetry axis passes through the vertex of a quadratic.

hints.title: Use contact with the axis
hints.body: A nondegenerate quadratic that touches the x-axis has a repeated root. Equivalently, its vertex height is zero.
hints.recap: Tangency to the x-axis gives a zero discriminant or a zero vertex height.
hints.pitfall: The constant coefficient in the given expression has a minus sign.
hints.pause: Use this contact condition to find the other parameter and evaluate the requested combination.

recall.reminder: Tangency to the x-axis gives a zero discriminant or a zero vertex height.

solution:
The axis is x=−62p=−3p. Setting this equal to −14 gives p=12. The curve is therefore an upward quadratic.

Complete the square: y=12(x+14)2−34−q. Its vertex lies on the x-axis precisely when −34−q=0, so q=−34. Equivalently, the zero-discriminant condition is 36+4pq=0.

Hence p+8q=12+8(−34)=6, option A. The resulting equation y=12(x+14)2 confirms exactly one x-intercept and the required axis.
knowledgePattern: Use quadratic axis and tangency together
